_metadata.independence: I read only x13-ra-input.json (plus this output file for a structural check) and opened no other file, repository search, web page or API.

hints.reason: ALIEN: the pop-culture alien spacecraft; SKY: UFOs are things spotted in the sky; an easy, clean scene clue, though the explanation states the alien-pilot trope as fact.
hints.fix: In stories, aliens fly UFOs across the sky.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; soften the explanation so it reads as the familiar trope rather than a fact.

hints.reason: BALL: the Snitch is the small winged ball in Quidditch; GOLD: it is the Golden Snitch; Harry Potter is mainstream enough and the aha lands well.

pairs.pair_note: Good pop-culture pick; both sides are named directly by the Golden Snitch.

hints.reason: GREEN: completes Green Day; BAND: Green Day is a famous band; it is a plain band-name join on a very common word, but Green Day is instantly familiar and the pair clicks the moment both words are seen together.

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable band-name phrase-join; DAY is generic, so this one sits near the line (one of three band-name joins in the batch).

hints.reason: JAM: completes Pearl Jam; BAND: Pearl Jam is a well-known rock band; a distinctive hint word that leads quickly to the band name.

pairs.pair_note: Band-name join, but Pearl Jam is famous and PEARL points at it more directly than DAY points at Green Day.

hints.reason: RAIN: "Purple Rain" is instantly familiar; BAND: only via Deep Purple or Prince's backing band the Revolution, and most players think of Prince as a solo artist, so the BAND side needs the explanation and two different routes.

pairs.pair_note: The RAIN side is excellent but the BAND side is a defended stretch; facts are correct (Purple Rain was credited to Prince and the Revolution).

hints.reason: BAND: bands play gigs; STAGE: a gig is a live show on a stage; a clear, easy scene clue.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair.

hints.reason: BASEBALL: a baseball bat; CAVE: bats roost in caves; a textbook double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, clean double meaning.

hints.reason: BEACH: a beach ball; DANCE: a ball is a formal dance (Cinderella's ball); a nice two-sense clue.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning with a fairy-tale flavour on the DANCE side.

hints.reason: BEAR: bears (and Winnie the Pooh) love honey; LOVE: "honey" is a pet name for a loved one; warm and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the two senses are distinct and both familiar.

hints.reason: BEE: bees sting; MUSIC: Sting is the famous singer of the Police; a good common-word/famous-name double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Nice aha; Sting is widely known to a U.S. audience.

hints.reason: BIRTHDAY: birthday cake; CUP: cupcake; both compounds are instant and the pairing feels natural (cupcakes at a birthday party).

pairs.pair_note: Easy phrase-join that works because both compounds are everyday words.

hints.reason: BIRTHDAY: birthday party; TEA: tea party (the Mad Hatter's tea party); both phrases are instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but fair phrase-join; the Mad Hatter's unbirthday tea party is a bonus resonance.

hints.reason: BOSS: the final boss; VIDEO GAME: "final boss" is a video-game term (and Final Fantasy is a famous series); fair, but the line overstates that all games end with one.
hints.fix: Many video games end with a final boss.

pairs.pair_note: Works; fix the VIDEO GAME line, and the explanation could mention Final Fantasy as a second route.

hints.reason: BRAIN: brainstorm; WEATHER: a storm is weather; clean and immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: CAMERA: a camera flash; LIGHTNING: a flash of lightning (and the Flash's lightning bolt); clear and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; both are bright bursts of light, which makes it feel neat.

hints.reason: CAR: car windows; COMPUTER: program windows on screen and Microsoft Windows; good, but "Computers run in windows" is muddled wording.
hints.fix: Computer programs open in windows (and many PCs run Windows), and cars have windows.

pairs.pair_note: Good idea; tidy the explanation.

hints.reason: CARD: hearts, spades and so on are suits; SPACE: an astronaut's spacesuit; two unrelated senses that click nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning.

hints.reason: CHEESE: the cartoon mouse-and-cheese trope; COMPUTER: a computer mouse; classic, though "a mouse loves cheese" states a cartoon trope as fact (real mice prefer grains and sweets).
hints.fix: A computer mouse, and cartoon mice love cheese.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and fair; minor wording softening only.

hints.reason: CHINA: the dragon is a national symbol (dragon dances, Chinese zodiac); KNIGHT: knights slay dragons (St. George); two very different cultural routes meeting on one creature.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; a satisfying East/West meeting point.

hints.reason: CIRCUS: circus clowns; FISH: clownfish like Nemo; easy and fun.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the Nemo line is a nice touch.

hints.reason: COMPUTER: Apple makes Mac computers; TREE: apples grow on trees; a well-worn but clean brand/fruit double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar and fair.

hints.reason: EASTER: the Easter Bunny; MAGIC: the magician pulling a rabbit out of a hat; both images are iconic.

pairs.pair_note: RABBIT beats BUNNY here because the magic-hat image uses "rabbit".

hints.reason: FAIRY: Tinker Bell lives in Neverland; PIRATE: Captain Hook's crew sails there; a place that naturally holds both.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent place-based clue; HOOK would cover only the pirate side.

hints.reason: FISH: starfish; MOVIE: movie star; both compounds are instant (the line wisely does not claim a starfish is a fish).

pairs.pair_note: Simple, fair phrase-join.

hints.reason: FLOWER: a flower bud; FRIEND: "bud" is slang for buddy; short, sweet and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; "best buds" even blends both.

hints.reason: FOOT: you stamp your foot; MAIL: a postage stamp; a clean verb/noun double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning.

hints.reason: FOOTBALL: John Madden and the Madden NFL football series; VIDEO GAME: Madden is a best-selling video game franchise; very familiar to U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: Good U.S.-specific pop-culture pick; the hint names one thing that is both.

hints.reason: GHOST: ghosts say "Boo!"; MONSTER: Boo is the little girl befriended by Sulley and Mike in Monsters, Inc.; a lovely aha twist on the obvious spooky route.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch: the obvious ghost route plus a Pixar payoff.

hints.reason: GOLF: a golf swing; PARK: the swings at a park playground; clear verb/noun double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: HAND: you wave your hand; OCEAN: ocean waves; immediate and clean.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: KING: a royal court; TENNIS: a tennis court (with Billie Jean King as a bonus); a neat, distinct double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the royal sense gives a nice aha.

hints.reason: KISS: kiss a frog to break the spell; PRINCE: the Frog Prince (and The Princess and the Frog); the popular telling links all three instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Strong fairy-tale clue.

hints.reason: LIFE: a 1-Up is an extra life; VIDEO GAME: the Super Mario green mushroom and arcade bonus; the digit spelling is conventional and the clue is fun.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; widely known from Mario.

hints.reason: MAGIC: casting a spell; SCHOOL: learning to spell (spelling tests, spelling bees), with Hogwarts as a bonus route; a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; both senses are distinct and familiar.

hints.reason: MIRROR: "Magic mirror on the wall" (Disney's Snow White); QUEEN: the Evil Queen consults her magic mirror and is herself a sorceress; the QUEEN side leans on the mirror but the Snow White scene clicks for everyone.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and familiar; the queen side is a little indirect but the scene is iconic. Quote is accurate for the Disney film.

hints.reason: NAIL: you hammer a nail; SHARK: the hammerhead shark; a nice aha on the shark side.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: NUMBER: you count numbers; VAMPIRE: Count Dracula, with Sesame Street's Count von Count uniting both; a delightful double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch; the Sesame Street Count is a perfect bridge.

hints.reason: WOLF: the Big Bad Wolf huffs and puffs; PIG: he does it to blow down the three little pigs' houses; the catchphrase calls up the whole story.

pairs.pair_note: Good fairy-tale catchphrase clue; the PIG line is bare but not wrong.

hints.reason: VAMPIRE: folklore vampires are repelled by garlic; PIZZA: garlic is a common pizza ingredient and topping; a fun pairing of the mundane and the spooky.

pairs.pair_note: Good; nice contrast between kitchen and folklore.

hints.reason: RED: Little Red Riding Hood; WOLF: the wolf she meets in the story; the hint word sits right in the title so the link is immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair fairy-tale clue.

hints.reason: SNAKE: venomous snakes bite with fangs; VAMPIRE: vampires' iconic fangs; a clean shared property.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair.

hints.reason: SPACE: the space station; TRAIN: a train station; both phrases are instant.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but fair phrase-join.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.
